source: Original (authored November 2026, no calculator, radians only). Unit circle labelled from memory at 16 standard angles; exact values; Pythagorean identity verified at 5pi/6 and used with a quadrant condition.

parts.label: a
parts.description: On the unit circle diagram, write the angle in radians (inside) and the coordinates (cos theta, sin theta) (outside) at each of the 16 marked points.
parts.tolerance: Accept 1/sqrt2 for sqrt2/2. Accept 2pi or 0 at the point (1, 0). Coordinates must be exact.
parts.notes: A1 for all 16 angles in radians at the correct points. A1 for the four axis points. A1 for each quadrant's three non-axis points (first, second, third, fourth), each needing both coordinates with correct values and signs. Angles in degrees earn the first A0. Wrong method: swapping the coordinates of the pi/6 and pi/3 points (or 7pi/6 and 4pi/3, etc.) earns A0 for that quadrant. The labels are written on the diagram inside the answer box.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down the exact values of sin(5pi/6), cos(4pi/3) and tan(7pi/4).
parts.tolerance: Exact values only. 0.5 and -0.5 are acceptable as exact.
parts.notes: A1 for each value. Bare answers earn the marks. Wrong methods, each A0: sin(5pi/6) = -sqrt3/2 (gave the cosine); cos(4pi/3) = 1/2 or -sqrt3/2; tan(7pi/4) = 1 (sign).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Verify sin^2 theta + cos^2 theta = 1 for theta = 5pi/6.
parts.tolerance: Accept sqrt3/2 without the negative sign, since it is squared.
parts.notes: Show-that part (AG). M1 for substituting both exact values into the identity. A1 for 1/4 and 3/4 seen, adding to 1. Writing only 'sin^2 + cos^2 = 1' with no values earns M0A0. A square of -3/4 earns A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Given sin theta = 2/3 and pi/2 < theta < pi, find the exact value of cos theta.
parts.tolerance: Accept -sqrt5/3 or -sqrt(5/9). A decimal earns the final A0.
parts.notes: M1 for cos^2 theta = 1 - (2/3)^2 (or = 5/9). A1 for +/- sqrt5/3 (or sqrt5/3 seen). A1 for choosing the negative value; a reason (second quadrant) is expected but not required for the mark. Final answer +sqrt5/3 earns M1A1A0. A correct final answer with no working earns A1 only. Wrong method: 1 - 2/3 = 1/3 (forgot to square) gives -1/sqrt3, earning M0A0A0.

source: Original (authored November 2026, no calculator, radians only). Plot y = sin x and y = cos x on a grid from unit-circle values; gradient of OP is tan(theta); lines from an angle with the x-axis (pi/6 with intercept 2; 2pi/3 through (1, 4)).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Plot y = sin x at multiples of pi/6 from 0 to 2pi on the grid, join with a smooth curve and label it.
parts.tolerance: Points within half a grid square.
parts.notes: A1 for at least 11 of the 13 points correct. A1 for a smooth curve (no straight segments, no corners at the maximum and minimum) labelled y = sin x. A curve labelled y = cos x earns the second A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: On the same grid, plot and label y = cos x in the same way.
parts.tolerance: Points within half a grid square.
parts.notes: A1 for at least 11 of the 13 points correct. A1 for a smooth curve labelled y = cos x. Curves labelled the wrong way round lose the second A1 in both (a) and (b).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Show that the gradient of OP, where P = (cos theta, sin theta), is tan theta.

expected.answer: (sin theta - 0)/(cos theta - 0) = sin theta / cos theta = tan theta

parts.tolerance: Accept a right-triangle argument (opposite sin theta, adjacent cos theta).
parts.notes: Show-that part (AG). M1 for rise over run using O and P. A1 for sin theta / cos theta seen before the given answer. Writing only 'gradient = tan theta' earns M0A0.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Line L1 makes an angle pi/6 with the positive x-axis and has y-intercept 2. Find its equation.
parts.tolerance: Accept 1/sqrt3 or sqrt3/3 for the gradient, and any equivalent form of the equation.
parts.notes: A1 for the gradient tan(pi/6) = 1/sqrt3. A1 for the equation. Wrong methods: m = sqrt3 (the value for pi/3) or m = sin(pi/6) = 1/2 earns A0 for the gradient, then A1 FT for y = mx + 2.
parts.follow_through: FT the equation from the candidate's gradient.

parts.label: e
parts.description: Line L2 makes an angle 2pi/3 with the positive x-axis and passes through (1, 4). Find its equation.
parts.tolerance: Accept any correct form of the equation.
parts.notes: M1 for m = tan(2pi/3). A1 for -sqrt3. A1 for the equation. Wrong methods: m = +sqrt3 earns M1A0A1 (FT); swapping the point's coordinates, y - 1 = -sqrt3(x - 4), earns M1A1A0. A correct equation with no working earns A1 only for the equation, plus A1 if -sqrt3 is seen.
parts.follow_through: FT the equation from the candidate's gradient.
